title: Morphisms from algebraic spaces to a fibred groupoid with representable diagonal
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ a category fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes, with the conventions for fibred groupoids and 2-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose that the diagonal $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\times_S\mathcal F$ is representable by algebraic spaces: its 2-base change by every $S$-scheme is equivalent to an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For every algebraic space $A/S$ and every morphism $a:A\to\mathcal F$, the morphism $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Explicitly, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and morphism $t:T\to\mathcal F$, the 2-fibre product $A\times_{\mathcal F}T$ is equivalent to an algebraic space over $T$. No stack condition or atlas for $\mathcal F$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), implication (1) => (7); (8) also gives the stated fibre products.

proof.text: Fix $S$-schemes $U,V$ and morphisms $x:U\to\mathcal F$, $y:V\to\mathcal F$. Form the scheme $W=U\times_SV$ using [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $b:W\to\mathcal F\times_S\mathcal F$ have components $x\operatorname{pr}_U,y\operatorname{pr}_V$. There is an equivalence $P=U\times_{\mathcal F}V\simeq D=W\times_{b,\mathcal F\times_S\mathcal F,\Delta}\mathcal F$ over $W$. Here is its full fibrewise verification using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Over a test scheme $R$, an object of $P$ is $(u:R\to U,v:R\to V,\phi:x(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}y(v))$. Send it to $(u,v,z=y(v),\alpha=\phi,\beta=1)$ in $D$, where a general object of $D$ is $(u,v,z,\alpha:x(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}z,\beta:y(v)\xrightarrow{\sim}z)$. Conversely send this object to $(u,v,\beta^{-1}\alpha)$. Over fixed $u,v$, an arrow in $D$ is $r:z\to z^\prime$ with $r\alpha=\alpha^\prime$ and $r\beta=\beta^\prime$; thus it exists precisely when $\beta^{-1}\alpha=(\beta^\prime)^{-1}\alpha^\prime$ and is then uniquely $\beta^\prime\beta^{-1}$. The composite on $P$ is the identity; the other composite is naturally isomorphic to the identity by the arrow $\beta^{-1}$ from the original object to its chosen representative. These formulas commute with pullback to $R^\prime\to R$, using the specified pullback coherence, and preserve the projections to $U,V$. Hence they give the asserted equivalence of fibred groupoids.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), proof of (1) => (3), displayed diagonal-base-change equivalence.

proof.text: By the hypothesis on $\Delta$, its base change $D$ by the scheme $W$ is equivalent to an algebraic space. Step 1 therefore makes $U\times_{\mathcal F}V$ equivalent to that same algebraic space, with its projection to $V$. Since $V$ and $y$ were arbitrary, the definition of representability by algebraic spaces in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] says that every map $x:U\to\mathcal F$ from a scheme is representable by algebraic spaces. This uses only the given diagonal tests, not descent for objects of $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), proof of (1) => (3), displayed diagonal-base-change equivalence.

proof.text: Now fix the given $a:A\to\mathcal F$ and an arbitrary scheme map $t:T\to\mathcal F$. Step 2 says that $t$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space] with its source $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{there}}=T$, target $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{there}}=\mathcal F$, morphism $f=t$, space $Z=A$, and map $Z\to\mathcal G_{\mathrm{there}}$ equal to $a$. It gives exactly $A\times_{\mathcal F}T$ as an algebraic space. Its projection to $T$ makes it an algebraic space over $T$. Since every scheme map $t$ was allowed, this proves representability of $a$, including the explicitly stated fibre-product clause. The cited lemma assumes only fibred groupoids, so no stack condition or atlas has entered.
